title: S14 e6.18 — the elliptic city (BSD island band 1)

concepts.name: the curve form: a curve over the rationals in the equation y squared = x cubed plus a x plus b, smooth exactly when four a cubed plus twenty-seven b squared does not zero out

lesson.statement: an elliptic curve over the rationals is the set of the rational points on the equation y squared equals x cubed plus a times x plus b, together with the point at infinity, and it is a curve exactly when four times a cubed plus twenty-seven times b squared does not zero out — on my line the panel holds two of them, the first with a is minus one and b is zero (of record), the second in the y squared plus y form with a is minus one and b is zero (of record), and the pair a is zero and b is zero zeros the discriminant out and is not a curve at all

concepts.name: the chord-tangent law: the points of a curve form a group — the line through two points meets the curve a third time, its reflection the sum; exact rational functions of the points

lesson.statement: the points of the curve form a group under the chord-tangent law: the line through two points meets the curve a third time, and that third point, reflected across the x axis, is their sum; the point at infinity is the identity; the law is exact over my rationals — for distinct points the slope is the change in y over the change in x, and a point with itself takes the slope three times x squared plus a over two times y plus the form's own constant — so every sum, double, and multiple I form is a rational point I can re-check against the curve's equation

concepts.name: the shadow count: for every prime of the line the curve holds its points over the field with p elements, counted exactly; from the count and the prime comes the coefficient a = p + 1 minus the count

lesson.statement: for every prime of my line the curve casts a shadow: its points over the field with p elements — a finite set, counted exactly by testing each x against the equation mod p — and I record the count for every prime on the line; from the count and the prime comes the coefficient a = p plus one minus the count, the coefficient of the curve's L-function at that prime

concepts.name: the shadow censuses: the Hasse bound held prime by prime on the line (a theorem of record, the census the verified shadow), and for the first panel member the record signature zero exactly when p is two or three mod four

lesson.statement: the shadow censuses of the band: the Hasse bound — a squared at most four p — is a theorem of record that my census verifies prime by prime on the line and does not prove; and for the first panel member the record signature — the coefficient is zero exactly when p is two or p is three mod four — is the shadow of the curve's complex multiplication, held on my line as the verified pattern, both directions, at every prime of the line

theorems.statement: the point at infinity is the identity of the group: adding it to any point is that point, and the law's own formulas hold it — every point I form on my line answers the identity exactly

the inverse of a point is its reflection: the point plus its inverse is the point at infinity, the line through them vertical, its third meeting the identity — every point I form answers exactly against its own reflection

the Hasse bound held on my line: for both panel members and every prime on the line, a squared is at most four p — the full prime by prime record, all passing, at the line end 84; the bound itself is a theorem of record, the census my verified shadow of it

the record signature held on my line: for the first panel member, its shadow coefficient at p is exactly zero exactly when p is two or p is three mod four — both directions, at every prime on the line, the all-pass record at the line end 84; the reason is of record, the pattern is the verified shadow on my line
